principles: Close ONLY the residual external-advance window; do not re-architect the already-correct main-write-lock serialization.
Fail closed: on a detected drift, abort BEFORE any phase mutation or merge, leaving the story exactly at TEST.
Keep the merge atomic and the lock handling unchanged; the re-check is a read-only comparison plus a throw.
Minimal blast radius: one guarded comparison in transition-orchestrator.ts plus one smoke; no other files.
Behavior-preserving for the happy path (main unchanged in-lock) and for all non-DONE transitions.
drivers: The main-write-lock already serializes concurrent Lattice DONEs (transition-orchestrator.ts ~311/319/473); the ONLY uncovered race is an external git advance between the pre-check sync and the in-lock merge.
A DONE persisted against a drifted main strands the just-re-established escalation verdicts and verification evidence (observed in B-12d7).
After-DONE auto-retry would need a partial-DONE state machine + rollback that does not exist and would lengthen lock holds toward the ~120s stale-reclaim threshold.

options.name: abort-before-persist-mainsha-recheck
pros: Closes the exact residual window with a cheap read + comparison.
Fail-closed: no partial DONE, story stays at TEST, operator simply re-runs.
Zero change to the lock or the merge; smallest blast radius.
cons: Requires the operator to re-run story_advance DONE on the rare external-advance (acceptable: fail-closed > silent drift).

options.name: after-DONE-auto-retry
cons: Needs a partial-DONE state machine + rollback that does not exist.
Lengthens lock holds toward the ~120s stale-reclaim threshold (risks a second DONE reclaiming the lock mid-merge).
Much larger blast radius for a rare race.

options.name: full-merge-serialization-rework
cons: The lock ALREADY serializes Lattice DONEs — this solves a non-problem.
Large, risky rewrite of a core gate for no added coverage of the external-advance window.

rationale: The lock already serializes Lattice DONEs; only the external-advance window remains. A post-lock pre-merge mainSha re-read compared right before phase=DONE persists closes exactly that window with a fail-closed abort, no lock/merge change, and the smallest possible blast radius. Auto-retry and a full serialization rework are both disproportionate to a rare race and add risk.

preMortem.scenario: The re-check captures the wrong baseline sha (before autoSyncMain, or after the merge), so it false-positives on every DONE or never trips.
preMortem.trigger: Capturing main sha at the wrong point in the sequence.
preMortem.consequence: Either all DONEs abort (broken) or the window stays open (no-op).
preMortem.mitigation: Capture main current sha IMMEDIATELY AFTER autoSyncMain completes (~325, the post-sync baseline) and re-read right before store.writeStory (~431); the smoke asserts both the abort-on-external-advance and the happy-path-no-abort.

preMortem.scenario: The abort runs AFTER store.writeStory persists phase=DONE, so the story is marked DONE but the merge is skipped.
preMortem.consequence: A worse state than the original bug: DONE with no merge.
preMortem.mitigation: Place the re-check strictly BEFORE actor.send/writeStory; the smoke asserts the persisted phase is still TEST after an aborted DONE and that no merge commit landed.

preMortem.scenario: The abort throw leaves the main-write-lock held, deadlocking subsequent DONEs.
preMortem.trigger: Adding bespoke lock handling around the re-check.
preMortem.consequence: Every later DONE blocks on the held lock until stale-reclaim.
preMortem.mitigation: Throw a plain error that propagates to the EXISTING try/finally (~536) which already releases the lock; add no new lock code.

preMortem.scenario: False positive when Lattice own autoSyncMain advanced main — aborting a legitimate DONE.
preMortem.consequence: Legitimate DONEs that needed a sync always abort.
preMortem.mitigation: Capture the baseline AFTER autoSyncMain so Lattice own sync is already reflected; only an external advance after that baseline trips the abort.
